narrative_before: Attackers compromised the update server of the Ukrainian accounting software M.E.Doc and added malicious functionality to its updates, rerouting update traffic through an attacker-controlled server in France that delivered NotPetya (DoJ indictment). On an infected host, NotPetya extracted credentials from LSASS with an embedded Mimikatz-style module, duplicated tokens, and moved laterally by writing to the Admin$ share over SMB (executing via PsExec/WMIC) and by exploiting the EternalBlue/EternalRomance SMBv1 vulnerability. It then wrote a custom boot loader that encrypted the Master File Table and overwrote disk sectors, rendering machines unbootable; the data was not recoverable. The June 2017 outbreak caused billions in global damage.

detection_moments.description: Supply-chain delivery: the M.E.Doc update server pushes NotPetya to subscriber hosts via the hijacked update channel.
detection_moments.evidence: 'Attackers added malicious functionality to the files containing software updates for M.E.Doc ... rerouted internet traffic ... to France-based server ... that delivered the NotPetya malware' - DoJ indictment / CTID flow

detection_moments.description: On-host credential/token theft and SMB/EternalBlue lateral spread, then MFT encryption and disk wipe rendering hosts unbootable.
detection_moments.evidence: 'logs into any version of SMB with the stolen tokens or harvested credentials and does a UNC write to Admin$ ... tests for vulnerable SMBv1 (Eternal Blue/Romance) ... custom boot loader encrypts the MFT' - CrowdStrike / CTID flow

attack_path: hijacked M.E.Doc update delivers NotPetya to subscriber host - T1195.002
SMB Admin$ UNC write + PsExec/WMIC using stolen tokens/credentials - T1021.002 / T1569.002
EternalBlue/EternalRomance SMBv1 exploitation of remote service - T1210
ambiguities: NotPetya spread automatically to 'known IP addresses and TCP endpoints / domain controllers'; specific internal hostnames are not named, modelled as dc, srv_1, pc_2, pc_3.
The malware both wipes (T1561.002/T1485) and 'encrypts' the MFT; highest on-host risk (9) applied.
No single defender detection moment in the flow; m1 = supply-chain delivery, m2 = lateral spread + destruction (the outbreak was self-evident on reboot).
